name: Matrix Transformation
description: You are given two matrices $$$A$$$ and $$$B$$$ of size $$$n \times m$$$, filled with integers between $$$0$$$ and $$$10^9$$$. You can perform the following operations on matrix $$$A$$$ in any order and any number of times: &= : choose two integers $$$i$$$ and $$$x$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$x \ge 0$$$) and replace each element in row $$$i$$$ with the result of the bitwise AND operation between $$$x$$$ and that element. Formally, for every $$$j \in [1, m]$$$, the element $$$A_{i,j}$$$ is replaced with $$$A_{i,j} \text{ & } x$$$; |= : choose two integers $$$j$$$ and $$$x$$$ ($$$1 \le j \le m$$$, $$$x \ge 0$$$) and replace each element in column $$$j$$$ with the result of the bitwise OR operation between $$$x$$$ and that element. Formally, for every $$$i \in [1, n]$$$, the element $$$A_{i,j}$$$ is replaced with $$$A_{i,j} \text{ | } x$$$. The value of $$$x$$$ may be chosen differently for different operations. Determine whether it is possible to transform matrix $$$A$$$ into matrix $$$B$$$ using the given operations any number of times (including zero).
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 100$$$) — the number of test cases. Then, $$$t$$$ test cases follow. Each test case is given as follows: the first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n, m \le 10^3$$$; $$$n \cdot m \le 10^3$$$) — the dimensions of the matrices $$$A$$$ and $$$B$$$; the following $$$n$$$ lines describe the matrix $$$A$$$, where the $$$i$$$-th line contains $$$m$$$ integers $$$A_{i,1}, A_{i,2}, \dots, A_{i,m}$$$ ($$$0 \le A_{i,j} \le 10^9$$$); the following $$$n$$$ lines describe the matrix $$$B$$$, where the $$$i$$$-th line contains $$$m$$$ integers $$$B_{i,1}, B_{i,2}, \dots, B_{i,m}$$$ ($$$0 \le B_{i,j} \le 10^9$$$).
output_specification: For each test case, output Yes if it is possible to transform the matrix $$$A$$$ into the matrix $$$B$$$; otherwise, output No . Each letter can be output in any case, upper or lower.
approach_summary: Maintain prefix sums and dynamic point updates via Fenwick tree using lowbit operations (i & -i) in O(log N) time and O(N) space.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2043E — Matrix Transformation [70. BIT / Fenwick Tree]
topic_editorial.summary: Point updates and range prefix queries with Fenwick Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every integer $i$ has a unique binary decomposition. Index $i$ in a Binary Indexed Tree stores the cumulative sum of the interval $(i - \text{lowbit}(i), i]$, allowing logarithmic traversal via $i \mathrel{+}= (i \mathbin{\&} -i)$ and $i \mathrel{-}= (i \mathbin{\&} -i)$.
